message.content: {"items": [{"hypothesis_id": "AND(SENSOR_BIAS,SPEED_STEP)", "rationale": "The combined sensor bias and speed step structure achieves the lowest RMSE among all single and paired models, indicating it best explains the small but consistent deviations between nominal and observed positions while the target remains continuously present.", "evidence_refs": ["obs:0:1.200"]}, {"hypothesis_id": "AND(SENSOR_BIAS,VELOCITY_OFFSET,SPEED_STEP)", "rationale": "The full three-factor model achieves the second-lowest RMSE, marginally higher than the two-factor sensor bias plus speed step model, suggesting no significant improvement from adding velocity offset.", "evidence_refs": ["obs:0:1.200"]}, {"hypothesis_id": "SENSOR_BIAS", "rationale": "As a single-factor model, sensor bias yields the lowest RMSE, supporting a constant position measurement offset as a primary contributor to the observed deviations.", "evidence_refs": ["obs:0:1.200"]}, {"hypothesis_id": "VELOCITY_OFFSET", "rationale": "Velocity offset performs well as a single-factor model, consistent with a steady belt speed deviation causing growing position error over time.", "evidence_refs": ["obs:0:1.200"]}, {"hypothesis_id": "SPEED_STEP", "rationale": "Speed step is a plausible single-factor explanation for a change in belt motion behavior during the observation window.", "evidence_refs": ["obs:0:1.200"]}, {"hypothesis_id": "AND(VELOCITY_OFFSET,SPEED_STEP)", "rationale": "This paired model accounts for both a constant velocity shift and a discrete speed change, fitting the data better than either factor alone.", "evidence_refs": ["obs:0:1.200"]}, {"hypothesis_id": "AND(SENSOR_BIAS,VELOCITY_OFFSET)", "rationale": "Combining sensor bias with velocity offset captures both a constant measurement offset and a steady speed deviation, improving fit over single factors.", "evidence_refs": ["obs:0:1.200"]}]}
